data.name: One More Night
data.detailed_description:
One More Night is a 4 player action packed top down shooter that will keep you on the edge of your seat struggling to survive just one more night! Get your team together, build towers, and prepare your defenses in an attempt to fortify your position as much as possible to protect yourself against the relentless horde of enemies!

Game play is split up between two phases; day and night. During the day, players will have a few moments to access the shop to buy weapons, ammo, and buildings to help them to survive the coming night. Once the night phase begins enemies will start to spawn and target the players and their buildings. Each additional player to the team causes more enemies to spawn each round. Additionally, each night will spawn more enemies and they will get progressively tougher every night. As the team survives more nights new, harder, types of enemies will start to spawn.

You will need to find out which strategies work best to survive as long as you can. Will you build a base and bunker down or will you try and out run the enemies until you die of exhaustion? The choices you make will dictate how long you and your friends survive.

Game Features

  • Up to 4 players in one game via online Co-op (Local offline coming soon)

  • In game shop with dozens of weapons, buildings, and defenses

  • 5 bonus skills to buy so you can survive as long possible

  • Steam trading cards, emojis, and backgrounds

  • Large map with 7 additional unlock-able areas

  • 7 skills to level up and give you extra power

  • Building and tower upgrades

  • Complete controller support

  • Character leveling system

  • 70 achievements

Community Discord

Have any questions, comments, or concerns? Our Community Discord is the best place to keep up to date on all the news and to suggest things you would like to see added to One More Night!

reviews.review:
[h1]One More Night[/h1]

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

One More Night is a top down shooter which puts you in the shoes of a survivor who is expected to survive One More Night against incoming waves of enemies like zombies and skeletons. 

On first glance, it seems like another game in the flood of zombie survival games on steam and it is exactly that. Let me make it clear in the very start that One more Night is exactly that. It does nothing to differentiate itself from the competition and it is not worth your time or money in its current state.

There are three characters to choose from in One More Night which differ from each other only in terms of their stats. Once you boot up a game, you are given a few seconds to prepare yourself for the coming night. There is no actual tutorial present here and One More Night desperately needs one. There is a very high learning curve present in the game and there is no exposition as to how to do anything as the game leaves everything to be figured out by you. 

Once the night starts, you are confronted by enemies who chase after you while you run around in circles and shoot them. This is basically all you do in the entire game, run around and shoot enemies. You can also build a few towers and barricades to escape the enemies but that is about it.

 Aside from the enemies, the game fills the whole map with poisonous gas a few moments into the first night because why not without giving any explanation on how to escape it. 
The weapon and enemy types are very limited and there is nothing present here that you would not have seen before. Even when the game does show a few sparks of potential, the amount of bugs present in the game totally kill the vibe.

 More than once my gun refused to fire even after clicking multiple times even when the clip was full leading to cheap deaths. The framerate took multiple hits randomly without any specific reason. There is an argument to be made that the game was made to play with friends but I cannot see myself enjoying this game even with a couple of friends.

 Early Access is a tag which can be used to excuse the game from the bugs but after this first impression, I am probably not going to return to survive One More Night unless something miraculous happens in the development.

[h1]Visuals[/h1]

The visuals present in One More Night are very drab. The map is one of the most uninspired ones I have seen in a long time. The only difference between day and night is the difference in contrast. The most horrific thing in the visual aesthetic should be the enemy design and the environments but in One More Night there is nothing more terrifying to look at than the characters on the character selection screen.

 Only time something visually interesting happened was when the poisonous fog filled the map. The zombies being flashed while there is an intoxicating green colour filled the map was one of the few moments I thought there was some potential here. Visually overall One More Night is not at all pleasing to look at.

[h1]Sound[/h1]

An average soundtrack is accompanied with some of the worst gun effects I have ever heard. More than sounding like a gun being fired, it sounds like a pellet gun. Aside from that, the usual grunts and moans of zombies make this a sound design which can be muted.

[h1]Overall[/h1]

I am one of those people who has not been touched by the zombie fatigue in gaming. Killing zombies never stops being satisfying for me but One More Night has way too many problems to make it a satisfying and brainless zombie killing experience. Being in early access, some of the minor problems of the game can be forgiven but on a platform with thousands of other games, One More Night does very little to deserve your time and money. 

[h1]Rating: 40/100[/h1]

This review was brought to you by [url=http://steamcommunity.com/groups/marvelousreviews] Marvelous Reviews[/url]
